description:
From the fz-kdt.143 refutation (2026-09-02, e3e82476c). The drop rule
(unroutable(N) <=> some W stands in for N and not seats_before(N, W)) is
proven arrival-relative except for ONE shape: a dropped arm N that shares its
runtime question with a SURVIVOR S. The seat moves whole question groups and
covers quantifies over the product, so N's narrow surface pins the group
{N, S} behind a wider arm W; drop N, the group dissolves, S is judged alone,
and precision seats S ahead of W. Values in the S/W overlap then reach S's
body where every arrival of the three arms sent them to W. Pinned by
a_drop_that_dissolves_a_question_group_reseats_the_survivor_it_pinned
(callsite_dispatch.rs): N = impl_two(%{a: int}, :a), S = impl_zero(%{a: int |
float}, :a), W = impl_two(%{a: int | float}, :a | :c); (%{a: 1}, :a) reaches
impl_zero after the drop and impl_two before it. Corpus: the precondition
occurs on ZERO callsites over 597 fixtures (instrumented sweep at the landing);
randomised search over 21,726 generated callsites found it 19 times and
nothing else (survivor set never empty, no precise live specialization lost).
fz-kdt.118's group-local drop had the same residue (dropping a member changes
the group's covers product).

WHY THE DISPATCH LAYER CANNOT FIX IT: the re-routed values lie in BOTH S's
and W's surfaces. When S and W are specializations of ONE callee the change
is meaning-neutral by construction (either body is a valid specialization for
a value its surface names) and the post-drop seat is the more precise one.
The change is meaning-bearing only when S and W are DIFFERENT callees --
i.e. the semantic layer offered two callees for one value at one callsite,
which is an ambiguity no seat can resolve honestly (arm order decided it
before; a rule decides it now). That is a semantic-layer invariant to state
and enforce: targets of different callees at one callsite must have DISJOINT
observable surfaces (protocol impls are keyed on disjoint types; measure
whether anything else can produce the overlap), or the overlap is a
diagnostic. Once that invariant holds, the residue is provably meaning-
neutral and the dissolution paragraph in callsite_dispatch.rs /
dispatch-matrix.md reduces to a statement about precision.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) a census gate over the corpus that no callsite carries two
callees whose observable surfaces overlap (or the diagnostic that names one);
(2) the residue paragraph rewritten to the same-callee case only.
title: A dropped arm that shares its question with a survivor dissolves the group and can re-route an overlap between two callees: the dispatch layer cannot decide which callee a value belongs to
